scope: External Python client and candidate core authoring responses; not a full API stability guarantee

linux.qualification: Final checkout CTest python_client_contract; 18 unittest cases

windows.qualification: Final checkout native Windows Python suite

native_behavior: All nine core methods with full/catalog/focused discovery
Standalone Unicode world paths, preview isolation, commit, exact retry, inspection and history
Parent filters, Transform reads, world matrices and revision-pinned pages
Shared host cross-client retries, stale mutation rejection and safe detachment
Historical receipt revision preserved after undo/redo and reopening
Accepted pre-history receipt replay preserves absent history metadata
synthetic_behavior: Reordered concurrent replies and exact request correlation
Structured native errors preserve a usable transport
Blocked pipe writes respect call deadline and direct child cleanup
Capacity, request size, JSON encoding and bounded stderr
Interrupt/write race preserves control flow and original recovery parameters
Wrapper snapshots cannot drift when caller or embedded transport mutates inputs
Unexpected core result retains the original receipt and does not retry
Independent malformed-response fixtures, additive metadata and bounded traversal
limits: The authoring contract remains candidate; no full engine/gameplay/renderer/save/ABI stability guarantee.
Synthetic transport failure tests and native retained-receipt checks are separate; no real crash-during-commit guarantee.
Direct child process cleanup is qualified; generic descendant-tree cleanup is not promised.
Python wrapper snapshot preparation occurs before the per-call transport deadline.
Only the recorded Python versions are executed; Python 3.9 is the package minimum, not a separately qualified runtime here.
Same-platform native clients are qualified; paths are not automatically translated between Windows and WSL.
Installed wheel is locally qualified, not published to PyPI; installed desktop package is unchanged.
GUI, GPU, provider-agent turns, scale/performance and public comparison benchmarks are outside this checkpoint.
